public_rationale: Read plainly, the claim says the price of OpenAI's and Anthropic's paid subscriptions does not cover the cost of providing them, and that the companies cannot fix this. The packet does not settle that. A secondary summary of The Information, published 2026-01-22, reports that Anthropic's 2025 margin on its paid-user business was a few points above 38% (e1). That is a positive figure. But the same summary says Anthropic expected about 86% of its 2025 revenue to come from the API rather than subscriptions (e2), so the figure does not isolate subscriptions. The summary also reports projected 2025 losses: an EBITDA loss of about $5.2 billion for Anthropic and an EBIT loss of $21.2 billion for OpenAI (e2). Those figures cover training and all product lines, not subscriptions alone. Neither company's subscription-level costs appear in the packet. On 2026-08-25, OpenAI restored a five-hour usage limit for ChatGPT Plus to spread out compute demand (e3). That falls after the target period and says nothing about price against cost. No item addresses whether a fix is possible.
limitations: The figures are estimates and projections from a secondary summary of press reporting. They are not audited disclosures.
Company-wide margins and losses do not isolate the consumer subscriptions.
The meaning of 'sustainable' (per-subscriber gross margin versus company-wide net profit) is the evaluator's choice.
The packet has nothing that tests whether a fix is impossible.

our_interpretation: Plain reading: at the time of the post, OpenAI's and Anthropic's paid subscriptions (ChatGPT Plus and Pro, Claude Pro and Max) cost more to provide at the service levels sold than they bring in at current prices. The companies also cannot close that gap without raising prices or cutting the service.

Target period: the claim describes the state at the post date (2026-04-14). The most recent public evidence on these economics covers 2025 and early 2026, so the period runs from 2025-01-01 to 2026-04-14. This choice is flagged as an ambiguity.
Evidence would come from press-reported or analyst figures, since neither company publishes audited unit economics for its subscriptions.
criteria.support_condition: Credible reporting shows that consumer subscriptions lose money per subscriber at current prices (cost to serve above price), with no workable path to fix this other than raising prices or cutting service.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible reporting shows that consumer subscriptions are profitable per subscriber at current prices, or that the companies made them sustainable without raising prices or cutting service.
